To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: It's official!! Fernhollow Photo is a real business

Okay. Doing this now, before Thanksgiving, so I don't have to do it over the turkey while Dad does his whole health insurance speech.

FERNHOLLOW PHOTO IS A REAL BUSINESS. Like, an LLC and everything. Filed October 22nd, website went live November 1st, and I have fourteen weddings booked for 2027. I typed that sentence and then had to go take a walk.

You all know I've been shooting for Rosebud Lane for four years. Marisol closed the studio at the end of October. She told me on October 6th — before she told anybody else — and she said she was going to send me every 2027 couple she couldn't keep. Six of my fourteen came from her. She had already told all six of them about me before I even knew she was going to. I keep thinking about that part.

The other eight found me on their own, which is the number that still makes me a little bit insane. The very first one that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken, June 12th at Timberline. They found me from the pictures I shot at Multnomah Falls for Marisol's couple. When they booked me I sat in my car and read their email six times.

Marisol basically taught me everything I know. Four years of standing at the back of her weddings with a flash and no idea what I was doing, and then one day she handed me a real camera and said "you'll love this," and she was right. She did not have to send me a single couple. She sent six. I'm going to be talking about this woman for the rest of my career.

And the reason she closed the studio is hers to tell, whenever she wants to tell it, and it is not mine to tell. So please don't ask me, and please don't ask her either. She'll say something when she's ready.

Now, the embarrassing parts.

I filed the LLC on my lunch break. In the parking lot of the Fred Meyer on 82nd, sitting in my car, and I cried a little. A woman walked past with a cart and I pretended to be looking at my phone. There was nobody there to take the picture. It was fine. It was a very good lunch break.

Sam made me a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLLOW. It spelled it FERNHOLOW. We ate it anyway, and at this point it's the official spelling. He keeps saying he'll make another one when I have a "real place," and I've told him I am not getting a storefront, Sam, it's a camera and a website, but he does not care about my business model. He is, however, an excellent cake baker, which is not the same thing and is more important.

The name is from Fern Hollow Trail, the little loop behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. It's all ferns and moss, and it takes about twenty minutes if you don't stop to take pictures, which I always did, because that's where I took my first real pictures with Grandma's old Pentax. I was so bad at it and so happy. Grandma, if you're reading this: the name is for you and for that trail. Every couple I photograph from now on is getting a business named after your backyard. I'm going to tell you in person, but I wanted it on the record first.

Dad: the health insurance is sorted. Marketplace plan, starts January 1st, I picked it out myself on November 5th and I have all the paperwork, so you can keep the speech short. You can still do the speech. I know it's a big part of the holiday for you.

If you're wondering whether I thought this through: I have. I've been building this in my head for two years, which is apparently a thing Marisol noticed, because when she told me she said "you've been ready for two years" and honestly I think she was right. And when I say I have a plan, I mean a plan and not a hope. LLC filed. Website live. Deposits paid on all fourteen, so these are real couples, not maybe-couples. Health insurance handled. Jae second shoots the big ones with me and he's paid per wedding, so it's professional and not a favor I have to owe forever. June is my busiest month with four weddings, and my furthest one is out at Wallowa Lake in September. If spring comes in slower than I want, I know how to pick up extra work. I didn't wake up one day and decide to do this. I had two years of Tuesdays.

Is it scary? Yeah. A little bit. But it's the good kind of scary, mostly the kind where you keep looking at your own calendar and going wait, that's my name on that. And I have a plan, and I've got a person second shooting with me, and I've got deposits in, and I've got insurance starting January 1, and I've got a website that is currently just me being excited about it. That's the whole thing. That's the business.

Last thing. Free family pictures at Thanksgiving. I'm bringing the camera, I'll do anybody who wants them, no cost, no obligation, no need to look presentable. Bring the cousins, bring the babies (Juniper especially, she is seven pounds of content), bring your in-laws if they want to be included. We'll do it after dinner when the light goes all golden and everybody's a little food-drunk and honest.

Thanks for all of you being my family and my first audience. I love you. See you at Ruthie's on the 26th, and yes, I'll have the camera, and no, I will not be charging anyone, Mom.

Bring the rolls.

— T

reasons: It reveals the private contingency plan to pick up extra work if spring inquiries are slow.
